slides.heading: while Loops
slides.body: while Loops is part of Indefinite Iteration. This short lesson gives you a practical Python idea you can understand, try, and reuse in simple programs.

slides.heading: Core Idea: while Loops
slides.body: A while loop keeps running while its condition is True. When the condition becomes False, the loop ends.

slides.heading: Real-World Analogy
slides.body: A while loop is like a fan that keeps running while the switch is on.

slides.heading: Example: while Loops
slides.code:
guess = "open"
while guess != "open":
    guess = input("Try: ")
print("Unlocked")

slides.heading: Key Rule
slides.body: Every while loop needs a condition that can eventually become False, unless you intentionally stop it with break.

slides.heading: Try It Yourself!
slides.prompt: Use a while loop that prints Go while count is less than 3.
slides.hint: Increase count inside the loop so it can stop.

coding_challenge.prompt_text: Print Loop twice using a while loop.
coding_challenge.hint_text: Use the idea from the lesson. Keep the code short, readable, and correctly indented.
